abstract: The Möbius strip and the bulk Möbius resonator are of great interest to specialists in optics, acoustics, and quantum physics. Despite the apparent simplicity of the object and numerous publications, the Möbius resonator, like a magic box, still holds many surprises. Here, we demonstrate experimentally, theoretically and with a simple illustrative example that in a "thin" Möbius resonator with an odd number of twists, the longitudinal wavenumber is determined by the additional phase shift π (traditionally called the geometrical Berry phase) only if the total transverse index of the photonic mode is odd. For an even index, the Berry phase is zero. We also discovered "topological" quasi-bound states in the continuum in Möbius resonators with a square cross-section; they differ from "ordinary" ones by the exchange of azimuthal indices of the interfering modes in the anti-crossing region. Finally, we demonstrate an example of resonant topology by determining the dependence of the Berry phase on the Möbius resonator geometry based on the frequency difference between the eigenmodes of planar ring resonators and those of Möbius resonators. The discovered effects significantly expand our knowledge of the topology of single resonators and promise new practical applications.
